import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/credit_fraud.csv')

# Convert 'is_fraud' to a categorical type with descriptive labels for better readability in plots
df['is_fraud_label'] = df['is_fraud'].map({0: 'Not Fraud', 1: 'Fraud'})

# Set up the matplotlib figure and axes for a 1x3 subplot layout
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(18, 6))

# Define a color palette for consistency
palette = {0: '#1f77b4', 1: '#ff7f0e'} # Blue for Not Fraud, Orange for Fraud
palette_labels = {'Not Fraud': '#1f77b4', 'Fraud': '#ff7f0e'}

# Plot 1: Distribution of Transaction Amount by Fraud Status
# Using kde=True to show density curves and common_norm=False to normalize each group independently
sns.histplot(data=df, x='amount', hue='is_fraud_label', kde=True, ax=axes[0],
             palette=palette_labels, common_norm=False, stat='density', alpha=0.6, bins=30)
axes[0].set_title('Distribution of Transaction Amount by Fraud Status', fontsize=14)
axes[0].set_xlabel('Transaction Amount', fontsize=12)
axes[0].set_ylabel('Density', fontsize=12)
axes[0].legend(title='Fraud Status', labels=['Fraud', 'Not Fraud']) # Manual legend for clarity with common_norm=False

# Plot 2: Transaction Counts by Hour of Day and Fraud Status
# Using multiple='dodge' to show bars side-by-side for comparison
sns.histplot(data=df, x='hour_of_day', hue='is_fraud_label', discrete=True, ax=axes[1],
             palette=palette_labels, multiple='dodge', shrink=0.8, stat='count')
axes[1].set_title('Transaction Counts by Hour of Day and Fraud Status', fontsize=14)
axes[1].set_xlabel('Hour of Day (0-23)', fontsize=12)
axes[1].set_ylabel('Number of Transactions', fontsize=12)
axes[1].set_xticks(range(0, 24, 2)) # Show every other hour for better readability
axes[1].legend(title='Fraud Status', labels=['Fraud', 'Not Fraud'])

# Plot 3: Transaction Type Counts by Fraud Status
sns.countplot(data=df, x='transaction_type', hue='is_fraud_label', ax=axes[2],
              palette=palette_labels)
axes[2].set_title('Transaction Type Counts by Fraud Status', fontsize=14)
axes[2].set_xlabel('Transaction Type', fontsize=12)
axes[2].set_ylabel('Number of Transactions', fontsize=12)
axes[2].tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45) # Rotate x-axis labels if they overlap
axes[2].legend(title='Fraud Status', labels=['Fraud', 'Not Fraud'])


# Add a main title for the entire figure
plt.suptitle('Credit Card Fraud Analysis: Key Feature Distributions', y=1.02, fontsize=18, weight='bold')

# Adjust layout to prevent titles/labels from overlapping
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 1, 0.96]) # Adjust rect to make space for suptitle

# Save the final figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
